previousContract.meaning: Preserves the sealed event decision and reveal fixtures; this version adds mark, blood-sacrifice and human shrine-pick actions.

source.meaning: Frozen product source for adapter fixtures only; not a balance or release verdict.

scope.game: original solo four-seat game with one human seat and three AI seats
scope.markTiming: AI marks are generated before the event; the human mark input appears after the event reveal in the current UI.
scope.markAction: One human declaration: null or one current market index.
scope.sacrificeAction: Repeated one-at-a-time bleed decisions before the compound sealed auction submission, bounded by the engine life floor.
scope.shrinePickAction: If a human is the eligible shrine winner, choose one currently open legend index after the engine computes the pending result.

fixtures.proves: The legal human actions are no mark or any current market slot; the first solo human observation shows mark participation indicators without exposing AI target slots and omits the not-yet-visible next-market preview.
fixtures.doesNotProve: Multi-human hotseat mark observations or event-night human/AI timing parity.

fixtures.proves: Repeated bleed/continue actions are bounded by the engine bloodlet flag, escalating cost and life floor; each bleed transition uses the frozen engine bleed function and records public life deltas.
fixtures.doesNotProve: Arbitrary interleaving with private bid drafts or a complete joint sacrifice-and-auction action tree.

fixtures.proves: An eligible human shrine winner can select exactly any currently open legend; the original finishShrines path applies the selection and awards the legend.
fixtures.doesNotProve: All automatic shrine, tithe, endgame, chance or night-transition branches.

nextEngineeringDeliverable.name: adapt automatic battle, settlement and cross-phase history
requirements: Compare automatic battle and settlement transitions with the frozen engine, including death sweeps, tithe, shrine release and endgame closure.
Carry each seat's prior observations and own actions across event, mark, auction, sacrifice and shrine-pick phases without exposing hidden state.
Represent the product UI's event-night mark timing explicitly and quantify its difference from the headless policy order before proposing any product change.
Prove complete chance support, cross-night state restoration, canonicalization, terminal/payoff mapping and a feasible solver scope before any pass claim.

gate.blockingReason: Mark, sacrifice and shrine-pick fixtures are partial. Other decision phases, automatic transitions, full recall, complete chance, cross-night restore, canonicalization, policy enumeration, terminal/payoff mapping and independent solver review remain incomplete.
